extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, trademark attorneys, counsel, and parties interested in USPTO disciplinary processes (OED/OED Director and USPTO officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation (exclusion on consent) and the types of practitioner misconduct alleged and considered by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27
rubrics_metrics.description: An Affidavit of Resignation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 must be submitted for approval; the Director reviews and may approve an affidavit to permit exclusion on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must show that consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, that the practitioner is aware a disciplinary complaint is pending and of the allegations, that the practitioner understands the legal and factual consequences (including relevant CFR provisions), and that the practitioner consents to exclusion. The Final Order here states the affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' (Examples in the affidavit: acknowledgment of pending complaint, specific factual allegations, and understanding of consequences.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory and regulatory authority to approve exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has authority under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the legal basis for accepting an affidavit and issuing a Final Order of exclusion; practitioners and counsel should cite these provisions when addressing the process or appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to publish Final Order and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the sample provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notification includes a FOIA-reading-room posting and an Official Gazette notice summarizing the facts and the regulatory provisions implicated; the notice must be materially consistent with the text in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — competent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must provide competent representation to clients; alleged violations include failure to provide competent representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conduct alleged as violating competence include taking over representation without proper client communication or supervision and allowing unqualified persons to perform legal services.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — keep clients reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep clients reasonably informed about the status of matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failures included not informing former attorney's clients that the respondent became their attorney or that the prior attorney was unavailable, and not communicating directly with clients regarding their trademark applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) — explain matters to permit informed decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must explain matters to the extent reasonably necessary to permit clients to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failures included not explaining trademark legal concepts to clients before filing trademark applications and relying solely on a client questionnaire without verifying accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations included providing false information to OED during its investigation and signing documents without client signatures; such acts are flagged as potential violations of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — prohibition on conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must avoid conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include conduct that undermines fair process or the integrity of proceedings; the Final Order lists conduct (e.g., unauthorized practice, failure to cooperate) alleged to be prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) — acts/omissions reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts and omissions that adversely reflect on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is applied to a range of misconduct types alleged in the complaint (e.g., failure to supervise non-lawyers, misrepresentations to clients or OED).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.503 — partner responsibilities for non-attorney assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: As a partner in a law firm, a practitioner must make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures giving reasonable assurance that non-attorney assistants' conduct is compatible with the practitioner's professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations included failing to supervise a paralegal who prepared, signed (for the attorney), and filed trademark applications and approved Examiner's Amendments without the attorney's direct supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — prohibition on aiding unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not aid non-lawyers in the unauthorized practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged examples: directing non-lawyer assistants to provide legal advice and services in trademark and patent matters, permitting a paralegal to sign the attorney's name and file applications, and allowing non-lawyers to approve Examiner's Amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(h) — limitation of liability agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners may not make agreements prospectively limiting the practitioner's liability to clients for malpractice when the clients were not independently represented in making the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: respondent attempted to limit his liability to a client for malpractice when the client was not independently represented; such clauses are impermissible without independent representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(c) — handling of prepaid fees and client trust accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must deposit legal fees and expenses paid in advance into a client trust account and withdraw them only as fees are earned or expenses incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct: requiring clients to prepay trademark fees and depositing the entire pre-paid fees and expenses into the practitioner's operating account before the fees were earned and expenses incurred is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) — duty to cooperate with OED investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failures included not producing requested documents, providing false information to OED, and generally not cooperating with the investigation; non-cooperation itself is a sanctionable violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited client-communication and intake practices (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not (a) take over representation without informing clients, (b) file forms (e.g., Revocation of Attorney) without clients' signatures, or (c) rely solely on a questionnaire without direct client communication or verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists these as factual allegations underlying the complaint: failing to inform clients they had a new attorney, signing and filing revocation forms without client signatures, not communicating directly with clients before filing trademark applications, and not determining accuracy of questionnaire responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited delegation and supervision lapses (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not direct non-lawyer staff to perform attorney-only tasks without proper supervision (e.g., preparing, signing, and filing trademark applications; approving Examiner's Amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include permitting a paralegal to prepare, sign the attorney's name, and file trademark applications without direct supervision and allowing a paralegal to approve Examiner's Amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for reinstatement applications (presumption of truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when the excluded practitioner applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application, that the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a binding procedural consequence of consenting to exclusion; practitioners should understand the presumptive effect on future reinstatement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 after exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 and 11.60 set out post-discipline obligations and reinstatement procedures; the Final Order expressly conditions exclusion on compliance with those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct that trigger disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factual behaviors that can give rise to a disciplinary complaint include taking over another attorney's clients while that attorney was suspended, failing to notify clients, failing to verify client information, aiding unauthorized practice, attempting to limit malpractice liability without client independent counsel, mishandling prepaid client funds, and obstructing investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order's recitation of allegations provides concrete anti-patterns practitioners must avoid; these examples illustrate how the regulatory provisions are applied in practice.
